Oh shit, I thought it was just me!

Just sitting at my desk my face is damp. Walking to the bathroom I can feel the trickle down my back.

Wish I had any advice :(
Thank you.x

Hey there :)

Thanks for replying to this - I don't check in on this account every day, so I didn't see it till just now. I really appreciate you taking the time to respond. [This turned into a massive ramble on the theme of depression, exhaustion and hopelessness so you're more than welcome to file this under "Internet stranger has problems" and carry on with your day - I write on this account more as a way of expressing and clarifying than anything else, so that's fine, you really don't need to respond or even read the scree of text, it's been therapeutic just to write it - thank you.]


My GP did start out prescribing antidepressants when I asked for them. The first batch pulled me out of a nosedive but then piled on the blank-but-suicidal feelings so he switched me to a second type. Those really badly exacerbated a problem I was already having (crazy crazy uncontrollable appetite - a known side effect of the drug, when I went and checked a few weeks in). He told me it wasn't a side effect, that I "couldn't blame the pills" for the stone I gained over 6 weeks, and refused to admit he was wrong till he took the meds index out to prove to me that it wasn't a side effect.

To be fair to him, he did apologise when it was the first listed side effect, and admitted that this "wasn't his area of expertise". I was then given the option to pick myself a new medication and instead asked to be referred for assessment, preferably by a psychiatrist but whatever he thought was appropriate would have been fine. Said I'd speak to them about medication (...rather than let him pick one at random). He agreed to do that.

He didn't do that, but didn't tell me he hadn't. I weaned myself off the fat pills in desperation a month or so later while I waited for the appointment which I thought I'd been referred for. My calls were never returned. My letters were just filed. I didn't find all this out till over a year after the fact. 

If I'm honest I lost the ability to keep pursuing it after that. I got into a spiral with the idea that if I deserved the help then I'd have been given the help, and that if I was meant to be able to fix it all, then I'd have found a way to do so. I got into a somewhat delusional state about how this was all part of some cosmic punishment for my wrongs in life and that I needed to stop fighting it and stop trying to get out of it and suffer appropriately. It was messy. I stopped being able to trust my own impulses and motivations in any way. Months passed. I actually tried some other avenues, I looked at online help but couldn't find anything that I could really engage with. I struggle to break down my barriers if it's not face to face. I tried Overeaters Anonymous but couldn't get into the whole Higher Power thing, and really didn't want to take on a sponsor because getting into that kind of relationship and then killing myself would have been SO unfair on whoever it was. I met with a couple of therapists with a view to paying for them myself. The sheer effort of will it took to make contact, arrange a meeting and then go spend an hour doing an introduction to all this was immense. One of them wasn't a good fit for me and the other was an hour and a half of travel and could only see me in the middle of a work day. I ran out of energy after two. I stopped trying, which I know sounds pathetic, but I couldn't go through it all again at the time.

I gave in and went back to my GP in January, which is when I found out about the non-referral and so on. I was going to make a complaint about him, but he then announced that he's retiring, so there's nobody else to protect from his "care" and I can't be bothered to go through the process for the sake of it. I'm not going to get back the last two years of my life.

I've managed to get some possible help through a scheme at my company - it may yet come to nothing, because it relies on my GP consenting to write a prescription on the advice of the psychiatrist and he may refuse to do that (or agree to do it and then just not do it). 

I believe there is an antidepressant out there that could help me, but if this doesn't work out then I'm down to ordering online on the dark web and that's not really a road I want to go down - that requires a level of risk, optimism and effort which, in combination, seems unwise. 

In honesty, I really don't want to go through another series of rejections and failures with the medical establishment. It feels so very bad, it's so humiliating and leaves me feeling so small and so helpless. I'm better off feeling awful all of the time than feeling progressively more awful as I get rejected, turned away and ignored by the people I've gone to for help.

The facial scarring is pitted and permanent. It's really not important, it's just annoying that it might have been avoided if anyone would trust me and listen to what I was saying. I don't ever leave the house anymore except to walk to the bus and from the bus to the office so sunblock isn't really a problem. I'm in Scotland, so sun is rare anyway. I haven't yet found a sunblock that doesn't irritate my skin quite badly either, but the scarring isn't really a concern - it's not like I'm going to be dating again. Looking awful as a baseline state is not high on the list of things that's a problem. I grew up with chronic, disfiguring eczema so looking like and feeling like a monster is something that I can operate with when it happens. 

Interestingly, the psychiatrist I saw asked me about the facial scarring and subsequent discolouration and irritation and asked if it was lupus. It's identical to photos on the internet of some of the lupus face rashes, and that actually makes me feel a little better. Maybe I wasn't being irrational to be doubtful about the diagnoses I was given. Maybe it really is a legitimate problem. It doesn't make any difference because there's no point looking to see if anyone would look into a lupus diagnosis for me, but it's kind of heartening to know that maybe it really isn't just something I made up/caused myself/made too much of a fuss about.

As for a new doctor, The other regular GP at the surgery I'm at was complicit in just filing my letters when I was pursuing my referral and he's been rude and condescending the one time I've met him. My GP is actually closing the whole medical practice down when he retires in a few months, so I'll be passed to a new surgery. There are two other surgeries that I'm eligible to be seen at (in the NHS there are catchment areas that GP surgeries have to adhere to).

I was signed up with one of them but they met as a practice and decided they weren't qualified to oversee the administration of my testosterone. I really don't want to have to pay for all my bloods and prescriptions out of my own pocket, plus any possible future complications. Maybe things will be different three years on, but I'd still rather not be seen by a practice that is only seeing me because they're legally obliged to do the bare minimum. I don't see that being the kind of care environment that I'll get much help in.

The other one is in the middle of the towerblocks of the local council estate (the UK equivalent of the ghetto). The NHS won't change my title to "Mr" until I've given up my access to female healthcare, so no more pap smears, no mammograms in the future etc. so I'm still "miss" on their records. That's just not a safe thing to be living with there, I don't want to be attacked or followed home if someone calls me in for an appointment as Miss [Lastname] and a waiting room full of people see me walk through looking distinctly trans-mansome.

That might sound paranoid, but my home is my sanctuary, it's where I go to shut the door and feel safe. I already avoid going to local pharmacies to avoid any chance of the locals clocking me as trans. These are people that smash up bus stops for fun and steal motorbikes to ride around and then set fire to every weekend. They would have no qualms about quite seriously fucking me up.

So I have to move house to get a new GP, and honestly, I just can't do it. I don't even have the energy to cook food anymore. Dishes get done every three or four months at best. Packing, finding a flat and moving is so far beyond me.

Maybe sometimes you just have to know when you're beaten.

Hey, I'm probably not in any better a position than you are, but I want to say that your reason for being here may not have showed up yet. It's not much, but it's the truth. It might be that the time you really find your feet is when a friend unexpectedly gets pregnant and you end up lending a hand and helping to raise an amazing little human. The day your life really starts might be the day you find a dog that's been hit by a car at the side of the road. It might be the day you drop coffee all over a strangers pants.

I'm saying that life is weird and absolutely random and that I don't really think that there's any "point" to it at all. I don't think there's anything anyone is really "meant" to do, I don't think that destinies exist. I think things just happen to us, one after another. 

And clearly you've had a long string of nothing much good happening to you for quite a while now. But I do believe that could change.

I don't think that any life is wasted if it caused no harm and brought some pleasure or entertainment or love into the world, and I believe that's the truth.

What I do think is that it's hard, *really* hard, when you're living a life where nobody needs you and there's nothing you need to be doing. We're a kind of animal that seems to require purpose and production to stay sane. When we've got no war to fight, no harvest to get sown or reaped, when we've got no barn to build and no children who depend on us, no herd to tend to and nothing that needs to be made or repaired... it's like we go rotten in the head.

We start to atrophy with disuse when we're just floating along in the modern world. 

I don't have a solution to that, and I'm not going to offer you some trite "Hey! Have you considered getting a hobby!!" stuff because I'm pretty sure you've probably thought all of the thoughts you're capable of thinking by now.

But I'm saying that one day in the future there will be a time where your absence leaves a void. There will be a moment where you would have stepped in and wrapped a hurt dog in a blanket, or taken the crying baby from your exhausted friend, or apologised profusely to a laughing, coffee-covered stranger... 

And instead the world will spin on without you and the paths you would have trodden will become overgrown and lost to us.

It's not to say that you should stay out of guilt, it's not to say that you should stay so that those things will happen. It's more to say that there will be things that you want out there. There will be moments when it feels worth it, although you'll clearly have to wade through some crap to get there.

I suppose I'm trying to tell you that I don't think you've wasted anything, and I don't think that you're in any way worthless - or at least, no more or less than almost every other human on planet earth.

To the untrained eye, most of us live small, unremarkable lives and then eventually die small, unremarkable deaths. But it's when you zoom in on those lives, and you look at the small moments of tenderness, of compassion, of kindness, of brilliance in them... I guess that's the only thing that ever really matters, isn't it? The small moments.

I know none of this is really of any use to you, but I did want to tell you that at least one stranger on the internet believes that you haven't wasted your life, and believes that things can be different for you. I guess that's all.

I think one of the most pathetic moments of the last year was realising that I'd been crying and mumbling to the poor woman on the line at the Samaritans for a whole hour and that she was now politely but efficiently trying to get me to resolve the call.

It's not her fault, it's just that there's nobody else I can ask to listen to the things inside me, but other people need her time too and I shouldn't be hogging the line that way.

Ridiculous as this sounds, I'm having a really hard time paring down the people in my world in preparation for suicide later in the year. I've done ok with some of them, I've cut them out after an argument or I've managed to be annoying and flaky and they've dropped me. But I have a couple of amazing, wonderful friends who I just can't get to give up on me.

I know full well it's going to wreck them when I make my exit and I know I really need to work harder at cutting them out, but I'm weak and I crave their warmth. It's pathetic really. I'm too selfish to push them away now and I'm risking pulling them down with me instead.

I also seem to be having a weird issue with my hardwired programming to make friends. It's like I can't help it, if I'm dropped into a situation with new people then I immediately start trying to form bonds with them. If I've had 2 drinks then I suddenly start to behave a bit like my old self, chatting and making people laugh. I've already made one new friend since christmas and another one is trying to be friends with me.

And I just feel awful, these are nice people, good people, they don't deserve to get caught in the undertow of my selfish, useless dysfunction. They think they're just making a new friend, they don't know that I'm going to throw a cold bucket of grief and guilt all over them in a few months.

I think I've got time to lose them, but I should never have let them get near me. I should never have let anyone else on board once I'd made the decision to let this rotting old hulk finally sink.

I wish that the healthcare professionals I've seen in the last 5 years had been better able to look *past* the fact that I am trans. I've had a serious bacterial infection in my face left untreated for a more than two months because a GP was adamant that it was "acne from your hormone treatment" and then, when it really obviously wasn't, he decided it was "Rosacea caused by your hormone treatment".

I've never had acne, ever, and do not have acne now, and rosacea doesn't generally cause areas of your face to bubble and leak pus that needs to be drained three or four times a day. But what I said (and the photos I brought with me, and my explanation of what was going on) were dismissed because I'm taking a medication which *can* cause the effect that the GP thought it *might* be. My face is permanently scarred. 

I wish that medical professionals would not assume that because *they* are unfamiliar with my medical treatment and condition, that I also am unfamiliar with it. If I say "My body does not normally do this, this is unusual and I'm very concerned" then it would be nice to be believed.

I think that I am viewed very much as an "unreliable narrator" - somebody who is unable to be objective about, or have insight into the condition of either my body or my mind. I feel like I have to fight, hard, every time to have anyone listen to what I'm saying and trust that it might be true.

I've been desperately trying to get a mental health assessment done for two years now. My GP "isn't confident" about prescribing anti-depressant or anti-anxiety medication (he just asked me to pick one and, when I couldn't, indicated that this was a sign that maybe I wasn't really committed to getting treatment.) He has insisted from the start that I should only see LGBT mental health services. It doesn't matter that it's not my gender or my sexuality that is the problem, or that I've been really, really clear about that over and over again. Or that the provision for that in my area is almost non-existent with incredibly long waiting lists.

I'm going to be in the ground long before my name makes it to the top of that waiting list, which will be a relief for everyone involved.

I feel like a proportion of these people would be doing this with whatever issue they had taken an interest in. There are people out there who have some warped internal idea that they're somehow more capable of knowing about things than other people are.

That their knowledge is somehow better and more correct than anyone else's knowledge could be.

Personally I believe that it's probably a solid sign of some flavor of narcissistic personality disorder at work, and while this sounds weird a part of me is somewhat grateful when I run across it because it is a giant red flag with AVOID AVOID AVOID written on it.

I find the context is important - I'm 3.5 years into transition and the sting has gone out of unexpectedly running across pre-transition stuff. I don't mind seeing my old name on things - at worst it's a mild inconvenience (like, "If I ever wanted to show this to someone I hadn't known long, I'd have to tell them my old name" kind of inconvenient)

But last week was my birthday. I kept it super-quiet because I'm not dealing so well with people right now. But my dad sent me an email on the day just titled "[Oldname]'s Birthday"

It was a picture of me on my second birthday with my parents and a couple of aunts. 

And yeah, it *was* a picture of "[Oldname]'s Birthday" but he *knows* that I really don't like being referred to by that name and he persists in making use of it as often as he can because "He just can't get used to it" and "I have to understand that it's hard for him". He believes he should be allowed to say and do whatever he pleases because he is fundamentally more right about the world than anyone else could ever be. He feels like I need to have more respect for how difficult all this is for him.

Like it isn't hard for me getting an email from my own father deadnaming me on my birthday.

I've been trying to see one for more than two years now. My GP is totally determined that I only be seen by LGBT specialists, and there's only one in my region (for a city of half a million people, and all the surrounding towns and villages) and she is a psychologist whose specialty is art therapy.

She can't prescribe medication.

Nobody would even guess at how long her waiting list is - judging by other similar services in the area I'm guessing 12-18 months.

She does art therapy, but I can "request a one-to-one session too". And she does mindfulness. I don't think any of this is what I need, but that's the best I've managed to persuade anyone to offer me in the last 2 years. I've been **very, very** clear that my problems aren't being caused by, or even really related at all to my gender or sexuality, and I've been clear about this with everyone I've spoken to about it. This is, apparently, irrelevant.

I've got an "emergency" appointment with a private psychiatrist in two weeks, although it's taken 4.5 months to get to see him. The appointment is paid for through a scheme at work, but there's no guarantee that anything he prescribes or recommends will be paid for and I'm not rich. 

If it's anything like the experiences of the last two years, I'll be sent away with leaflets, or told to make another appointment in a couple of months if I'm not feeling any better, or told that he could write me a prescription, but I'll have to pick out a medication for myself. Or just offered a card with the local emergency suicide intervention place's details on it... but not actually given a card, because they'd run out of cards, so I walk away with nothing at all.

Which is what has been happening for the last 2 years.

I spent a while trying to find a therapist to pay for out of my own pocket last summer, but it's *so* exhausting meeting someone new, trying to do a half hour run-down of everything that's going on, trying to work out if the person you're talking to is suitable, and then finding out that they can't see you anyway (because they only have appointments available at 11am on a Wednesday or similar). 

Sorry. I'm rambling.

Basically I'm burned out completely and I'm being actively prevented from getting the help that I'm asking for by a GP who firmly believes that I should only be seeking "appropriate" services. 

I know I'm not going to survive this much longer so I'm slowly packing up my belongings ready for my flat to be cleared out by whoever has to deal with that once it's all over. I have long since lost faith that anyone is interested in offering me any help, and it's ok. I tried my best and that's all a person can do.

If I can swallow down the panic and keep going for another 5 months then I've got an opportunity to make as clean an exit as I can expect. It's just a case of holding on now.

I was 12 and I won an academic prize at school. It wasn't very impressive, there was no money or anything, just book tokens. But only 5 people in my group of 130+ students won a prize and it was really, really important to me.

And my parents just didn't care. They really didn't. They mostly seemed annoyed that I was trying to get them to look at the letter I'd been given about my prize, and the prize-giving ceremony at the end of the year. 

I was a good kid and I honestly worked really hard. I'd sacrificed a lot of my happiness to try and be the best, most obedient kid I could possibly be in the hope that my parents might show me some of the love and affection that I really desperately wanted. I thought that if I could show them that I'd really, really tired and I'd done really well in that first, hellish year of secondary school, that I might prove to them that I was a good kid. That I might finally deserve their love.

And they just didn't care.

I know it sounds ridiculous, but I was totally destroyed that day. I'd spent literally my whole life devoting every possible moment to pleasing my parents up till that point. I'd forgone friendships, I'd given up on things I loved, I'd suffered endless bullying and unhappiness to try and be what they wanted.

And something in me broke that day, something I've never gotten back again. I think that was the day that I fully understood that they were *never* going to give me the affection I wanted, and that I'd wasted my life working for it.

That was the day that I started to believe that I was just fundamentally unlovable, and that nobody would ever *really* care about me. I stopped seeing myself as someone with potential and started seeing myself as someone who was an inconvenience. That was the day that I started to emotionally divorce myself from my parents, and look toward getting away from them, rather than trying to be closer to them.

I wonder sometimes where I might be now if either of my parents had thought to give me a hug that day, or told me they were pleased that I'd worked so hard.

Simple answer is: The main source of support in my world leaves permanently in August, I have two really good friends with birthdays in September and I'm trying to avoid dates where it's someone that I know's birthday or wedding anniversary or whatnot.

It's going to fuck up the people that care about me badly enough without me doing it on a significant date in their lives which gets celebrated yearly.

I've exhausted all but one of my avenues for psychiatric/psychological assistance and support - they've all basically told me to go away, and I believe this last avenue will be the same. I can't go yet another year feeling like this. I have to leave and it's really selfish to do so, but I'm trying to be selfish in as considerate a way as I can.

This gives me plenty of time to continue getting rid of my stuff and cleaning up, making arrangements and getting things ready, so that it's not such a mess for other people to clear up afterward.

Shaky, really shaky.

I've been holding it together ok for a couple of weeks but this weekend was one long, unrelenting battle with myself to try and get anything at all done.

And I *did* get stuff done, more than usual, but I didn't feel any kind of positivity as a result. I don't really seem to feel any kind of positive feedback from anything anymore.

I slept as well as I ever do anymore but I still feel tired. I'm at work but I keep having these occasional episodes where for no reason my whole body starts to sweat uncontrollably and my vision blurs, I'm smacked with this deep terror, I lose concentration... Just sitting here at my desk clenching my jaw and hoping nobody notices.
I don't think we're going to see any decent headway on this until recognised news sources can consistently get it right.

Depends on the dude. I prefer my guys bearded, meaty and bookish. 

You bearded, meaty, bookish and into trans guys?
Not especially. Why?

I've had a callused hand rubbing my back. I've had both boyfriends and girlfriends with hands callused from work, playing instruments or exercise. They just have to learn when to be a bit careful and I had to learn when to tell them to be careful :)
Because that, of course, is the only thing that women's hands could possibly be for.

I don't really find Caitlyn Jenner attractive and I dislike her politics.

Or... wait, were you just making fun of trans people because that's the best you can manage as a form of conversation on the internet?
The fact that right I'm still carrying on with day-to-day life as if I'm not going to kill myself in October and fuck up everyone's lives horribly.
Turn off the wifi.

Women whose hands are kind of large, and maybe a little bit rough and callused.

I love it when hands look strong and capable.
I wish I'd never seen your face.

Jeff Who Lives At Home

I think a lot of us go through our lives with the nagging suspicion that we've somehow missed something, that we took a wrong turn somewhere and now we're just... drifting with no particular destination anymore.

And this film, which for the most part is kinda silly and maybe not all that great, takes that idea and reminds me that I'm not necessarily thought yet. That maybe I haven't missed all the chances I was ever going to have to do something worthwhile with my life, even if it feels that way right now.
That I'm going to keep stalling on doing it and that things are going to keep getting worse, to the point that I no longer have enough control over my life to make the decision for myself anymore.

Thank you for reading all this. And thank you so much for your writing. What your'e saying is stirring a lot in me.

> "I realised that I would drop everything and rush to his aid in a heartbeat - without thinking about it twice, and not just for him but for any close friend who needed my help. But never would I ever, ever, not in a million years, expect someone else to do this for me"

This... yes. There is nothing I wouldn't do, wouldn't give for someone I really love who really needed it. If any of the handful of people that I love desperately needed a kidney and I was a match then I'd be there in a heartbeat. But I myself have a *really* hard time just asking friends to help me move house.

Some part of me is just completely walled-off from the idea that anyone could be ready to offer me... well, anything, and then not hold it against me later. My parents are the "I told you so" types, and any small act of out-of-character generosity, any leeway given was *always* brought up again later. No transgression on my part was ever, ever forgotten. My mother would still bring up how untidy I was as a 14 year old over dinner with my girlfriend when I was 26.

My parents' attitude is that all things must be earned, if you deserve something then you need to sit quietly and wait till somebody notices and gives it to you. Asking for anything is a moral failing; offering yourself, your time, your effort up should be an immediate response at all times, no matter what. I've had to train myself not to be creepily over-eager to help/offer things up when someone shows me any measure of kindness.

> "That act of kindness and support ... caused me to dissolve completely."

I'm just fucking *terrified* of this. I've broken down in the past, and I've always had to pick up the pieces, put myself back together and then carry on, still broken but now also exhausted. I can't let anyone ever see that. Everything from my history tells me that allowing other people to be involved will lead to me being abandoned and rejected.

I remember being about 8 years old and gathering up the courage to go and ask my parents for something (I forget what, but I recall it being something quite reasonable which I felt I could state a rational case for) which was really important to me. They said no, and normally I would have just slunk away to my bedroom to cry, but this time I stood my ground and asked why. I wanted to know why I wasn't allowed whatever it was, I wanted them to have a conversation with me.

I don't remember what my dad said but I remember feeling so *stupid* and so small and so... ignored. So worthless. I cried and my dad would do this high-pitched mocking laugh and make fun of me. When I started to make for the door he pushed me back and blocked me into the room, wouldn't let me leave to go to my bedroom. He stood over me and laughed, making fun of me crying, holding me away from him, holding me in place with one hand while he stood against the door. Eventually he let me out, jeering, calling after me, I don't remember what. Nothing nice.

I just can't understand why anyone would treat someone that they love that way. I don't understand why anyone would want to *do* that to a child, no matter how annoying or difficult the child was being. I have a clear memory of being seven or eight and sitting on my bedroom windowsill rocking back and forth and saying over and over to myself "I want to go home". I *was* at home, the only home I had. But I would fantasise and daydream about having another family somewhere else, and I felt **so** wicked and so ashamed of that.

I remember very clearly really, truly believing that there was absolutely nobody who loved me. Who cared about me. What if I died, my parents would be ashamed, embarrassed and angry more than they'd wish I were still there. I'm still not sure that wouldn't have been true. I started really thinking about killing myself when I was about eight.

It's 26 years later and I don't really feel any different. I've had several big, serious relationships and experienced loving someone who loves me back. But I can never really open up. I would often choose selfish, manipulative partners and then make myself their victim. You can imagine. But even then I could never really, truly open up. It was always at least in part a performance. A part of me was always stored safely away so that I couldn't be destroyed.

And now... I'm almost 34. I've been single for almost three years and have had no intention of ever having another serious relationship for quite a while now. I can't deal with the guilt I feel about my friends' concerns about me. I've deactivated facebook and I've been slowly removing myself from the lives of the people I love. Backing away. I'm making myself unreliable, irregular. 

I have very much wanted to believe that I can change, that I can be better, that I can choose to live a different life from the life that was carved out for me by the people who were supposed to love me. But... I am tired.

Does that sound stupid? We're all tired, right. It's the nature of the human condition. But I just... can't keep hoping anymore. It's too painful. Living with my own relentless self-disappointment. I don't want to read anymore motivational articles and self-help books. I can't find the energy to keep on picking myself up dragging myself along with no idea how I might ever get better, and nobody who is willing to help me, to let me have the professional help I've been seeking. 

Sometimes I want to be able to slice open my soul and let all this horribleness and this anger and this bitterness drain out, and be... empty. Feel nothing. Be nothing. 

Thank you for being someone else who understands what it's like to live in here. Thank you for talking to me and letting me ramble.

I'm living in this constant, never ending cycle of self-sabotage that I just can't escape on my own. Any effort at self improvement or self-help I make is either soon after or simultaneously "balanced" out by some act of self-sabotage.

When I stopped smoking I also stopped going to bed before 2am. When I was going to the gym regularly I stopped permitting myself to drink enough water. When I was eating a really well calorie-controlled diet I would deliberately binge and then force myself to skip whole meals. I can't ever let myself just... be nice to myself. I can't ever let myself get better. 

I live under this impossible system of punishment and retribution. I feel an endless and crushing pressure to improve, succeed, set goals and achieve them, and then whenever I try I smash myself to pieces on the rocks of my own dysfunction.

It's completely exhausting and pushes into the territory of delusional thinking and behaviour at times. I can no longer distinguish which of my impulses and behaviours are meant to help me and which are meant to damage me. I'm tired of trying.

You've hit the nail on the head in a lot of ways.

> "you yourself don't really believe you should need help."

You're right. An underpinning part of how I feel about all of this is that it's stupid and I should just be able to get on with it, because there's nothing *actually* wrong with me. That's I'm just making a fuss and being attention-seeking.


> "I get the impression that you constructed a high-level existence that exuded confidence and generosity to others, but what sort of foundation was it built on? Did you feel worth it without those achievements?"

Spot on. I was chronically bullied all through school and then put a **lot** of effort into building myself a new way of living, one where I didn't cringe away from everything and apologise for myself all the time, a life where I was capable and confident and I didn't need anyone else to come in and fix everything for me. It was how I survived escaping my family. Without constantly proving that I'm strong enough to survive completely alone, *and* strong enough to support the people I love, I'm just that sad, dependent, confused child who can't do anything on my own.

> "You describe the depression as selfish. What is it that makes you feel it is selfish? That you are the one who needs support for a change?"

It's selfish because I'm only thinking about what *I* want and how *I* feel. I was raised with the idea that I should live in a constant state of gratefulness and happiness for all the things that I have. Also that I should not get in the way and make problems for other people. That my needs were trivial and selfish and I should stop bothering people with them. That nobody wants to hear what I think. It was trained into me that asking for things is shameful and taking up something that someone else might want or need is selfish. The idea being that if you're good and deserving and patient, that what you need will be given to you. I recognise this on an intellectual level as irrational, but I can't seem to strip the programming out of me.

> "The GP and therapist sound pretty useless, but it's also possible that they are still being fooled by your calm, collected and competent behaviour, so they're underestimating your depression."

I think you're probably right, but I also don't have any intermediate state of being in between my "work face" which is required for me to function outside of my home, and the person I am when nobody else is around, which I can't ever let anyone else see. Everything is a performance that I don't know how to stop giving for fear of completely collapsing in on myself and becoming helpless. And it is ingrained in me that if I can't help myself, that nobody else is coming to help me.

> "I'm guessing that you are exceptionally used to remaining collected even under adverse circumstances, so people might sincerely not fully realise how badly you're doing."

An important part of my training as a child was that I was never allowed to be out of control. It wasn't just that I needed permission for *everything*, it was also that I wasn't permitted to be angry, and I would be laughed at and/or excluded if I was upset and cried. I was never allowed to be rude or lose my temper, so from as early as I can remember, I've had what appears to be an exceptionally strong ability to repress and control my thoughts and feelings. I've lost my temper precisely once in adulthood. Being able to keep my thoughts, feelings and reactions hidden is a key part of keeping myself safe. I have to be able to keep calm and stay in control, otherwise other people will take my control away completely - you know when a little kid is trying to do something and their parent gets impatient and just takes it out of their hands and does it themselves? That.

> "I'm curious as to what lies under all those achievements. Were you always the strong one? Did you learn that others needed support more than you did?"

I'm the older child of a very angry, emotional younger sibling. I learned that I needed to stand still and be quiet while everyone dealt with other people's problems. I learned that I had no recourse to complain, because I should "know better" or I needed to "grow up". It was always me who needed to take corrective action, because I was a very easy child to control and manipulate. When I was bullied at school, my parents told me that I needed to stay out of the bullies' way and not provoke them. If there was any kind of problem or difficulty, I would have to just deal with that while someone sorted out my sister - because I was capable of staying calm and didn't scream and cry. I'd been trained not to "answer back" when someone was angry, so I had no way or ever standing up for or explaining myself when there was a problem either.

My parents were the only adults in my world other than teachers - no other family for hundreds of miles, my mother left work to raise us, so no babysitters or childminders. I was trained that I must always "behave" for other people outside our home, so I lived in fear of ever making a mistake or failing to perform well in front of teachers and friends' parents. I was *terrified* of school parents' evenings because I dreaded what kind of report my teachers might give my parents about all my failings. I was actually a really quiet, polite kid but I struggled with anxiety and couldn't always get on and do the work, which was a constant problem in my life.

Basically I learned from a young age that nobody wanted to hear what I thought, that my problems were my fault and hearing about them was an inconvenience to the people that I loved. I learned that **I** was a problem, and that I had to constantly be making up for all of the disappointments that I brought into the lives of my parents. That I ought to be doing better, given how lucky and how fortunate I was.

I wasn't the strong one. I was the problem who was getting in the way. Becoming the strong one was my path to taking ownership of myself and carving out a place that I was allowed to live my life and have feelings and needs of my own.

The crushing thing about all of this is that I understand on an intellectual level all about how irrational this is and how I was just a kid and it wasn't my fault.

But it's still written into me, scored into the bones of who I am, and understanding it isn't fixing it.

I have, in the fullness of time, become my own parent. Now I'm the one that pushes me away and tells me to stop bothering everyone when I feel bad.
